summary: Settlement processing stalled because the order-service v2.16.0 deploy (dep-6010, 07:40Z) changed the OrderExecuted event schema (qty->quantity, v2 header) on the shared Kafka topic, while settlement-service still expects schema v1; the poison message at orders-3@8841207 fails deserialization, is retried indefinitely with "partition blocked", so partition 3 never advances and lag grows monotonically. Timeline evidence is tight: throughput collapsed inside the 07:40Z bucket (F1, F2) — the same bucket as the deploy — and the first deserialization error appears at 07:42:14Z pinned to that single offset (F4, F5, F9). The competing config-change hypothesis (cfg-3004, max.poll.records 500->200) is weaker: it predates the first error and the mechanism (a smaller batch size causing rebalances) is counter-intuitive, and broker/dependency evidence is clean (under_replicated_partitions 0, DB pool flat, HTTP error rate flat). Confidence is medium (0.60 per the reviewed ranking), capped by an unverified producer side and one single-partition sample.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.16.0 schema change broke settlement-service deserialization on partition 3
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-6010 on order-service v2.16.0 (07:40Z) renamed qty->quantity and bumped the event schema header to v2 on OrderExecuted events published to the shared kafka topic. settlement-service still expects schema v1 and fails to deserialize ('missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'). The first failing offset (orders-3@8841207) blocks partition 3 permanently ('partition blocked'), so the consumer stops committing and processing that partition entirely — zero settlements, lag grows monotonically. Other partitions/consumers are unaffected in the sample, matching a single-poison-message stall rather than a systemic throughput reduction.

causal_chain.claim: order-service deploys v2.16.0 at 07:40:00Z, renaming qty->quantity and adding a v2 schema version header to OrderExecuted events
Settlement-service throughput collapses and lag begins rising in the 07:40 bucket, immediately after the deploy
Consumer logs deserialization failure 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' and then 'poison message ... partition blocked' on the same offset
The poisoned offset orders-3@8841207 never advances, permanently blocking partition 3 and preventing any settlement from that partition
Because partition 3 is never processed but the producer keeps publishing, consumer lag grows monotonically to ~60k
No downstream dependency failure explains the stall: DB pool flat, HTTP error rate flat, broker under-replicated partitions 0

assumptions: That the malformed v2 message actually originated from order-service's deploy rather than an out-of-band producer (gap: producer side unverified; no producer publish-rate metric retrieved)

That 'partition blocked' halts all settlement processing rather than just that one partition's records — the report says zero settlements, implying either a single-partition topic or a global commit halt
That settlement-service did not already tolerate v2 schema (no evidence of a consumer-side schema upgrade)

ranked_hypotheses.title: cfg-3004 consumer.max.poll.records=200 reduction causes group instability / rebalances that stall processing
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The only settlement-service config change in the window (cfg-3004, 07:35:37Z, max.poll.records 500->200) altered poll behaviour such that consumer heartbeats/processing exceed max.poll.interval.ms or the group churns through rebalances, so partitions are repeatedly revoked and never processed; lag grows because partitions never complete a processing cycle.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-3004 applied at 07:35:37Z reducing max.poll.records from 500 to 200
Reduced poll batch size / altered poll cadence triggers rebalance or heartbeat timeout in the consumer group
Partitions are repeatedly revoked, so no partition is ever processed to completion and throughput falls to zero
Lag accumulates monotonically because the producer keeps publishing while the consumer makes no progress

assumptions: A smaller max.poll.records would actually trigger rebalances — mechanism is counter-intuitive (smaller batches ease max.poll.interval pressure, they don't worsen it)
That the observed error signatures are coincidental rather than causal

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka broker-side partition reassignment / infrastructure failure stalls the settlement consumer group
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A broker-side event (partition reassignment, ISR shrink, or broker overload) around 07:40-07:42Z caused the settlement consumer group to stall on partition 3, producing growing lag and zero settlements, independent of the two code/config changes. This mirrors historical incidents HIST-112 and HIST-104 with infrastructure_failure root causes.

causal_chain.claim: A broker event (reassignment/rebalance) occurs around 07:40Z, coinciding with lag onset
The settlement consumer group loses/stalls partition 3, halting settlement processing
Lag grows monotonically as the producer continues publishing

assumptions: A broker-side rebalance happened but left no trace in under_replicated_partitions or cpu metrics
Only rests on UNVERIFIED historical incident leads (F17), which are explicitly not evidence about this incident

ranked_hypotheses.title: Downstream dependency (ledger-db) degradation blocks consumer mid-processing, lag grows independently of changes
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A downstream dependency settlement-service writes to (ledger-db) is degraded, so the consumer blocks mid-processing on the failing offset and partitions stop advancing; lag grows because processing cannot complete. This is the 'stuck consumer independent of config' theory, aligned with HIST-111 (past ledger-db slowdown affecting settlement-service).

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db (shared, platform-owned) becomes slow or unresponsive around 07:40Z
Settlement consumer blocks on the DB write and cannot commit offsets
Lag grows monotonically and settlements are not posted

assumptions: ledger-db slowness exists despite no evidence; DB pool_in_use flat and connection-pool 'healthy' line argue against it
Error messages would be DB/timeout errors, but observed errors are deserialization/poison-message — mechanism mismatch

facts.statement: Settlement throughput collapsed to zero inside the 07:40:00Z bucket: request_rate fell from ~60-63 req/s (07:00-07:35) to avg 25.87 at 07:40 and avg 0.41 at 07:45, staying at ~0.40 req/s through 09:55.
Consumer lag was baseline (~39-50 msgs) through 07:35, jumped in the 07:40 bucket to avg 515.03 / max 1306.47, and climbed monotonically to avg 60220.76 by 09:55 (summary max 61605.53).

The only deployment across 06:00-09:59Z was dep-6010 on order-service v2.16.0 at 07:40:00Z, changing the OrderExecuted event schema: qty->quantity rename, added venue, and a v2 event schema version header; status 'live', not rolled back.

The earliest error is a deserialization failure: at 07:42:14Z 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)', repeated 213 times; a second signature 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt n), partition blocked' appears from 07:44:51Z with 196 occurrences and is still occurring at 09:58:31Z.
All error signatures in the sample are pinned to a single offset on partition 3 (orders-3@8841207); no other partition id appears and the log explicitly states 'partition blocked'.
The first failing offset never advances, and the errors began at 07:42:14Z / 07:44:51Z, i.e. before the reported ~08:22Z onset.
The only config change in the incident window (and across 06:00-09:59Z) was cfg-3004 on settlement-service: consumer.max.poll.records changed 500->200 at 07:35:00Z by m.das.
Kafka broker health is clean: under_replicated_partitions is 0.0 for every 10-min bucket from 07:30 to 09:50Z.

settlement-service shows no DB/connection-pool pressure and no HTTP 5xx spike: db_pool_in_use flat ~5.2-6.8 connections across 07:30-09:59Z, HTTP error_rate flat ~0.18-0.26%, and a 'connection pool stats: healthy' INFO line at 07:53:07Z.
order-service is the upstream producer into the shared Kafka topic that settlement-service consumes, and both Kafka and ledger-db are shared platform-owned components.

assumptions: That the malformed v2 message actually originated from order-service's dep-6010 deploy rather than an out-of-band producer — the producer side was not verified and no producer publish-rate metric was retrieved.

That 'partition blocked' halts all settlement processing rather than only partition 3's records — the report says zero settlements, implying either a single-partition topic or a global commit halt; the exact mechanism was not confirmed.
That settlement-service did not already tolerate the v2 schema (no evidence of a consumer-side schema upgrade was checked).
That the config change cfg-3004 (max.poll.records 500->200) is coincidental rather than causal, based on timing (4 minutes before the first error) and on the counter-intuitive assumed mechanism.
That the error-log sample (40 earliest lines / 409 ERROR entries) is representative of the ongoing failure across the whole stall window.
That the deployment/config inventory (06:00-09:59Z) was complete enough to exclude other tracked changes.

timeline.event: settlement-service consumer lag flat/near-zero (~48 msgs); DB pool flat ~5-6 connections; pre-change steady state.
cfg-3004 applied to settlement-service: consumer.max.poll.records changed 500->200 by m.das; only config change in the window.
dep-6010 goes live on order-service v2.16.0: OrderExecuted schema change (qty->quantity, add venue, v2 header) on the shared Kafka topic.
Settlement throughput collapses inside this bucket (request_rate 60-63 req/s -> 25.87 -> 0.41) and consumer lag jumps from baseline to avg 515.03 / max 1306.47.
First deserialization error: 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)', eventually 213 occurrences.
'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt n), partition blocked' begins (196 occurrences), confirming the offset never advances.
settlement-service logs 'connection pool stats: healthy'; DB pool remains flat, HTTP error_rate flat — rules out pool exhaustion / DB-timeout mechanism.
Incident INC-010 reported by on-call SRE: no settlements for ~40 minutes, consumer lag growing, poll settings changed shortly before.
Consumer lag at avg 60220.76 (max 61605.53); throughput still ~0.40 req/s; no recovery in window. Kafka under_replicated_partitions 0.0 throughout 07:30-09:50Z.
Same deserialization/poison errors on orders-3@8841207 still being logged — the stall is ongoing and unmitigated.

recommended_actions.action: Immediately roll back or revert dep-6010 on order-service (v2.16.0 -> prior version) so the producer emits schema v1 OrderExecuted events again, then confirm the settlement consumer resumes past orders-3@8841207 and lag begins to fall.
recommended_actions.rationale: The first failing offset (orders-3@8841207) matches the v2 schema change in the same 07:40Z bucket as the throughput collapse; reverting the producer removes the poison message at source without touching consumer state.

recommended_actions.action: If a full order-service rollback is not possible quickly, make settlement-service backward-compatible for the v2 schema (accept 'quantity' as alias for 'qty' and accept the v2 header) as a stop-gap, then skip/dead-letter the single poison offset orders-3@8841207 so partition 3 can advance.
recommended_actions.rationale: The stall is a single blocked offset; allowing the consumer to tolerate v2 or to skip that one record unblocks partition 3 and stops the growing lag immediately.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT revert cfg-3004 (consumer.max.poll.records 500->200) as the primary mitigation, and avoid re-applying further poll-setting changes as a first response.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-3004 predates the first error by ~4 minutes and the error signatures are deserialization/poison-message, not rebalance/commit errors; changing it back would add churn without addressing the blocking offset.

recommended_actions.action: Replay/reprocess the order-executed records published between 07:40Z and the fix, after confirming the producer emits v1 (or after the consumer tolerates v2), and reconcile settlements for the gap window against ledger-db.
recommended_actions.rationale: Throughput was ~0 for the whole window (F1), so a backlog of unprocessed settlements exists and must be posted; ledger-db is a shared downstream that receives both order-service and settlement-service writes.

recommended_actions.action: Verify recovery by confirming: partition 3 advances past offset 8841207, consumer lag returns to baseline (~50 msgs), request_rate returns to ~60 req/s, and the deserialize/poison error signatures stop appearing in settlement-service logs.
recommended_actions.rationale: These are the exact signals that inverted at onset, so their inversion confirms the root cause and closure.

recommended_actions.action: Add contract/schema compatibility checks (producer/consumer schema registry or CI contract tests) gating any event-schema change on the shared Kafka topic, so a producer rename like qty->quantity cannot go live while consumers expect v1.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failure was a cross-service schema contract break with no gate; the shared-topic dependency was visible in the topology but not enforced.

recommended_actions.action: Add a consumer-side poison-message dead-letter path (bounded retries then DLQ + partition advance) and an alert on lag with a per-partition blocked-offset detector, so a single unprocessable record cannot silently stall settlement for 40+ minutes.
recommended_actions.rationale: A single offset blocked partition 3 indefinitely with no automated escape and the incident was only noticed ~40 minutes later at 08:22Z, despite errors starting at 07:42:14Z.

data_gaps: Producer side unverified: no order-service logs (WARN) or producer publish-rate metric was retrieved, so it is not directly confirmed that order-service's dep-6010 emitted the malformed v2 message rather than an out-of-band producer.

No Kafka broker/partition logs or rebalance metrics were obtained (broker exposes only cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions), so a broker-side reassignment (H3) cannot be positively excluded from metrics alone.

Error-log sample is limited (40 earliest lines, 409 ERROR entries) and only shows partition 3; it is not confirmed whether the topic has multiple partitions and whether other partitions/consumers were truly unaffected or merely absent from the sample.

Downstream ledger/posting health could not be checked: ledger-service and posting-service do not exist in this environment (query_metrics returned not_found), and order-service/ledger log queries were cut off by budget, so blast radius on downstream ledger/posting is unconfirmed.

The exact mechanism by which 'partition blocked' halts ALL settlement processing (single-partition topic vs global commit halt) was not established, so the path from one blocked offset to zero settlements relies on the reported symptom.
No consumer-group/offset-commit telemetry was available to show directly that commits stopped at orders-3@8841207.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Direct evidence that the v2/quantity messages on orders-3 were published by a producer other than order-service dep-6010 (out-of-band producer), which would break the causal link to the deploy.
Finding settlement-service already accepts schema v2, or that the failed offset was a one-off malformed record unrelated to the schema rollout.

Evidence of a Kafka broker partition reassignment, ISR shrink, or broker overload coinciding with the 07:40Z lag onset (e.g. rebalance counts, broker logs), which would support H3 (infrastructure_failure) over H1.
Evidence that the lag/zero-throughput stall occurs on multiple partitions or is driven by consumer-group rebalances rather than a single blocked offset, which would support H2 (cfg-3004) over H1.

Evidence of ledger-db latency/timeouts or DB errors on settlement-service mid-processing at 07:40Z, which would support H4 (dependency failure) — currently argued against by the flat DB pool and healthy pool log line.
Logs showing rebalance/commit/heartbeat errors (rather than deserialization/poison-message errors) at onset, which would reframe the failure as a poll-setting/group-instability problem.

findings.statement: Settlement throughput collapsed to zero inside the 07:40:00Z bucket: request_rate fell from a stable ~60-63 req/s (07:00-07:35) to avg 25.87 at 07:40 and avg 0.41 at 07:45, then stayed flat at ~0.40 req/s through 09:55 — i.e. zero real throughput persists for the whole window, ~42 min before the 08:22 report.

Consumer lag was flat/baseline (~39-50 msgs) through 07:35, then jumped in the same 07:40 bucket to avg 515.03 / max 1306.47, and climbed monotonically every 5-min bucket thereafter to avg 60220.76 at 09:55 (summary max 61605.53). Lag growth therefore begins at the 07:40 bucket, not at 08:22.
A config change was applied at 07:35:37Z (cfg-3004, consumer.max.poll.records=200) — ~4 min before the first error and the lag jump. It is the only config-change log line in the 07:30-08:30 window.

The earliest error is a deserialization failure, not a rebalance/commit/pool error: at 07:42:14Z "failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)", repeated 213 times (first_seen 07:42:14Z). A second signature, "poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt <n>), partition blocked", appears from 07:44:51Z with 196 occurrences.

refs.quote: failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)
poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt 92490), partition blocked

findings.statement: All error signatures are pinned to a single partition: every one of the 40 earliest error lines references offset 'orders-3@8841207' (partition 3). No other partition id appears in the sample, and the log explicitly says 'partition blocked'.

Settlement-service shows no DB/connection-pool pressure and no HTTP 5xx spike: db_pool_in_use flat ~5.8-6.2 connections across 07:00-09:55, and error_rate flat ~0.17-0.27% throughout. A 'connection pool stats: healthy' INFO line appears at 07:53:07Z. So the failure is not pool exhaustion or DB timeouts.

settlement-service consumer lag was flat/near-zero (~48 msgs) at 07:30Z, then rose monotonically every 10-min bucket: 1572 at 07:40, 5930 at 07:50, 10371 at 08:00, climbing to 59267 (max 61605) at 09:50Z. No recovery in the window.

settlement-service logged only ERROR-level entries (409 matched, all ERROR) starting 07:42:14Z, in two patterns: deserialize failure 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' on orders-3@8841207 (213x) and 'poison message: retrying ... partition blocked' on the same offset (196x), still occurring at 09:58:31Z.

refs.quote: failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)
poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt 92490), partition blocked

findings.statement: Deserialization/poison errors first appeared at 07:42:14Z and 07:44:51Z, i.e. BEFORE lag reached 1572 (07:40 bucket) and well before the reported ~08:22Z onset; the first failed offset is pinned to orders-3@8841207 and never advances.
settlement-service DB connection pool is NOT saturated: db_pool_in_use stays flat at ~5.2-6.8 connections across 07:30-09:59Z (first 6.0, last 5.91, max 6.78), with no rise at lag onset.
settlement-service HTTP error_rate stays flat ~0.18-0.26% throughout (min 0.1, max 0.32) with no spike at lag onset; consumer-side failures are not reflected as HTTP 5xx.

Kafka broker health looks clean: under_replicated_partitions is 0.0 for every 10-min bucket from 07:30 to 09:50Z (min/max/mean all 0.0). Kafka's only exposed metrics are cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions.

The only config change across all services in the incident window was cfg-3004 on settlement-service: consumer.max.poll.records changed from 500 to 200 at 2026-05-12T07:35:00Z by m.das ("Smaller poll batches to smooth DB writes"). A wider 06:00-09:59Z query returned the same single change.

The only deployment in the window (and across 06:00-09:59Z) was dep-6010 on order-service v2.16.0 at 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z, changing the OrderExecuted event schema: rename qty -> quantity, add venue, and a v2 event schema version header. Status 'live', not rolled back.

refs.quote: "OrderExecuted event: rename field qty -> quantity","add field venue","event schema version header v2"

findings.statement: settlement-service consumes from kafka (queue-consume) and writes to ledger-db (db). Both kafka and ledger-db are marked shared=true, owned by platform.

order-service is the upstream producer into the shared kafka topic settlement-service consumes: order-service -> kafka (queue-produce), and order-service also writes to the same shared ledger-db (db edge).

Two historical incidents with matching 'settlements stuck / consumer lag growing' symptoms (HIST-112, HIST-104) had infrastructure_failure root causes from Kafka partition reassignment, not from config or schema changes. HIST-111 shows a past ledger-db slowdown affecting settlement-service. Stated by the tool as leads, not evidence about the current incident.

findings.statement: The two concurrent changes are ~5 minutes apart (cfg-3004 at 07:35:00Z, dep-6010 at 07:40:00Z), both shortly before the ~08:22Z report of a ~40-minute settlement gap. The order-service schema change (qty->quantity rename, new v2 header) alters the event format consumed by settlement-service on kafka, co-occurring with the settlement-service poll-batch reduction.
